extracted.intended_audience: general readers, TV viewers, fans and researchers looking up information on the sitcom Roseanne
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and judge factors used in the article to assess the revival and historical success of the television sitcom Roseanne, including critical reception, ratings, awards, distribution, and controversies that affected renewal/cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotten Tomatoes consensus / critical reception
rubrics_metrics.description: "Roseanne's return finds the show's classic format, original cast, and timely humor intact, even if the latest batch of episodes suffers from sporadically uneven execution." (Rotten Tomatoes consensus; approval rating of 69% based on 80 reviews, average rating 6.72/10.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a qualitative summary of critics' views; includes the approval percentage, number of reviews, and average numeric rating to quantify consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metacritic weighted score
rubrics_metrics.description: Metacritic assigned the season a score of 69 out of 100 based on 31 reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A weighted-average aggregator score indicating overall critical favorability; used alongside Rotten Tomatoes to gauge critical response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nielsen ratings and delayed-viewing metrics (Live, Live+3, Live+7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiere seen by 18.45 million live and same-day viewers; gained an additional 6.59 million via Live+3 (totaling 27.26 million overall) and a net increase of 8.81 million over the week; set records for largest total-viewership increases in Live+3 and Live+7 metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative audience-measurement metrics (live and time-shifted viewing) are used to judge popularity and commercial impact; season averages and weekly ranks (Nielsen rank) are also cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and nominations as success indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Emmy Awards (Barr and Metcalf wins), Golden Globe wins for Barr and Goodman, Peabody Award, People's Choice Awards and multiple nominations across years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry awards and nominations are treated as markers of critical/industry recognition; the page notes specific wins and the overall tally (e.g., 27 Emmy nominations including revival).

rubrics_metrics.name: Home media completeness / edits (uncut vs. edited releases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchor Bay initially released the first season with shorter, syndicated versions and later rectified releases; seasons 8 and 9 have some scenes altered to avoid music-rights disputes; Mill Creek later re-released seasons uncut (first seven seasons uncut).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completeness and fidelity of DVD/streaming releases (uncut original broadcasts vs. edited versions) are presented as part of the show's legacy and archival quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syndication and distribution presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Off-network syndication beginning in 1992; carried on TBS, Nick at Nite, TV Land, Oxygen, CMT, Logo TV, Laff, later returned to CMT/Paramount Network/TV Land and is available on Amazon Prime Video, Hoopla, Pluto TV, Cozi TV, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued presence in syndication and streaming platforms indicates enduring demand and accessibility; the page also documents when networks dropped the show (e.g., Viacom pull) and later restorations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cast continuity / return of original cast
rubrics_metrics.description: The revival's success is linked to the return of the show's original cast and the show's classic format; the Conners spinoff was ordered involving every original cast member except Roseanne Barr.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention/return of core cast members is treated as a positive factor for revival authenticity and audience interest; casting changes or absences (e.g., Barr's exclusion) affect retooling decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topicality and timeliness of humor / addressing current issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Consensus notes the revival retains "timely humor"; Barr stated the show would continue to address current U.S. issues, hoping to "open up civil conversation between people instead of just mudslinging."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A show's engagement with current political/social topics and 'timely' jokes is presented as a criterion for relevance, but also a potential source of controversy and polarized reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creator/performer public conduct affecting network decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: ABC terminated Roseanne Barr after a racially insensitive tweet about Valerie Jarrett; network president called Barr's remarks "abhorrent, repugnant and inconsistent with our values." Episodes and campaigns were pulled from streaming and networks following the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public statements and social-media behavior by show creators/lead performers can directly influence renewal/cancellation, distribution, and public relations; networks weigh conduct against corporate values and commercial risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial/financial considerations (advertising revenue and scheduling)
rubrics_metrics.description: ABC emphasized Roseanne's success during upfronts; cancellation raised questions about potential repercussions for the network due to loss of advertising revenue and fall-schedule planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Networks factor expected ad sales, upfront promises, and scheduling when assessing a show's value; commercial implications can shape decisions independent of critical response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and political polarization in reception
rubrics_metrics.description: The cancellation sparked a divide among conservatives and others — some labeled it political correctness and an infringement on free speech while many commentators condemned the remarks; public debate influenced discourse around the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience political alignment and public controversy are documented as shaping the narrative around the show and influencing downstream effects (support, backlash, calls for cancellation, defense by public figures).
